newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Cabinet hold 2nd term skull session.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Cabinet hold 2nd term skull session.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and his incoming and outgoing Cabinet officers staged a day-long skull session on Saturday to discuss plans and objectives for Clinton's second term.
The closed event was largely a session for Clinton to familiarize himself with his nominees for Cabinet positions who, when confirmed by the Senate, will lead the departments of his government.
The Cabinet retreat was staged at the presidential guest residence, Blair House, under tight security on Pennsylvania Avenue across from the White House.

It included discussion of the U.S. budget; national security and how to preserve America's leadership role in the world; the global economy of the post-Cold War era and how to improve U.S. economic growth and expand trade; and domestic policy, including environmental preservation.

"This is an opportunity for the president to get together with all of his senior advisers today -- his incoming ones and the ones that are leaving in order to review the agenda over the next several months and into the second term, to get prepared to make decisions and to set priorities," said a White House spokesman, David Johnson.

Clinton crossed Pennsylvania Avenue to Blair House on a chilly, snowy morning without an overcoat and teased reporters about standing around out in the cold. Along the avenue much work was in progress building grandstands for parade viewing when Clinton is inaugurated for his second term on Jan. 20.
"I wish I had some news to make to compensate for your cold. Maybe I'll fall on the ice," he said, extending his arms forward and gazing down at his feet.

It was the first and probably the only get-together for the outgoing and incoming teams. It had originally been planned as a weekend conference at the presidential retreat at Camp David, but was moved to Blair House and reduced to one day. Aides said two pro football championship games to be televised on Sunday was a factor in truncating the schedule.

The long guest list included outgoing Secretary of State Warren Christopher and the nominee to replace him, Madeleine Albright, as well as outgoing Defence Secretary William Perry and his designated replacement, Republican William Cohen.

Vice President Al Gore also attended, as well as outgoing White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta and his replacement, Erskine Bowles. Bowles' deputies John Podesta and Sylvia Matthews were also there.
Aides expected the discussion to be fairly broad and doubted any hard and fast decisions would be made.

"This is not where he is going to check a bunch of boxes for Cabinet officers to go forward and do A, B and C," said one aide. "He will review with them the challenges that he will face and begin to set the agenda for the forthcoming term."
To prepare for the session, Clinton's incoming and outgoing national security team spent some time on Friday reviewing their presentation to the president, officials said.
